items.hook: The Indianapolis Motor Speedway opens for automobile racing. William Bourque and his mechanic are killed during the first day's events.
items.body: The Indianapolis Motor Speedway is a motor racing circuit located in Speedway, Indiana, United States, an enclave suburb of Indianapolis, Indiana. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: Pope Pius II is elected the 211th Pope.
items.body: Pope Pius II, born Enea Silvio Bartolomeo Piccolomini, was head of the Catholic Church and ruler of the Papal States from 19 August 1458 to his death in 1464. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: War of 1812: American frigate USS Constitution defeats the British frigate HMS Guerriere off the coast of Nova Scotia, Canada earning the nickname "Old Ironsides".
items.body: The War of 1812 was a conflict initiated by the United States against the United Kingdom and its allies fought mainly in North America and at sea during the wider Napoleonic Wars. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: Salem witch trials: In Salem, province of Massachusetts Bay, Martha Carrier, George Jacobs Sr., John Proctor, John Willard, and clergyman George Burroughs are executed after being convicted of witchcraft.
items.body: The Salem witch trials were a series of hearings and prosecutions of people accused of witchcraft in colonial Massachusetts between February 1692 and May 1693. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.body: For 46 years, he presided over Maison D'Orsay, a Paris perfumery. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: White Shark is a 1994 novel by author Peter Benchley, famous for Jaws, The Island, Beast, and The Deep.
items.body: White Shark is similar to Jaws but does not feature a shark, let alone a white shark, despite what the title suggests; the phrase is the codename of a weapon. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: In the wake of the murder of Julius Caesar, his nephew and heir, Octavian, uses the threat of military force to compel the Roman Senate to elect him Consul.
items.body: Gaius Julius Caesar was a Roman general, statesman, and author who was the dictator of the Roman Republic almost continuously from 49 BC until his assassination in 44 BC. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: Tenderenda the Fantast is a novella by the German writer Hugo Ball.
items.body: Set in fantastical locations, it consists of episodic chapters and functions as an allegorical story about the creation of the Dada movement in Zurich and Ball's eventual disillusionment with it. One of those things you can't un-know.
